newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUGUST 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUGUST 11.

text.p: PRAVO - The unemployment rate in July increased to 4.34 percent, the second highest since 1989, and is growing, according to a representative of the Ministry of Labour and Social Affairs. Unemployment peaked at 4.40 percent in 1992.

- Recent flooding in Moravia and Silesia has disrupted some regions to such an extent that roads and communitites are still threatened by the possibility of landslides, according to the manager of the environment section of the regional administration in Vsetin.

- The number of divorces in the Czech Republic has increased regularly over the last four years according to information from the Czech Statistical Bureau. In 1993, 30,227 marriages ended in divorce compared to 33,113 last year.

- The increase in natural gas prices currently being considered for October 1 is the result of the crown's weakening against the US dollar, according to Miroslav Tvrznik from the Ministry of Trade and Industry.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - July's increase in consumer prices is the largest in the last four and a half years. Prices increased on average by 3.5 percent over June. The main cause was a number of recent deregulations in rent, electricity, natural gas and heating costs.
- The Ministry of Finance will issue the second tranche of flood bonds worth 1.2 billion crowns.

- British Airlines and Saab are willing to offer Aero Vodochody a license to manufacture their Gripen fighter aircraft if they are chosen by the Czech government to supply the aircraft, according to the director of British Airlines for Europe and North America, Alan Garwood.

- The main problem facing the acceptance of foreign aid for the recently flooded areas in Moravia and Silesia is a lack of information regarding concrete needs of these regions, according to Jan Kasal, vice-chairman of the Christian Democratic Union.
MLADA FRONTA DNES - According to a recent survey by GfK, Czechs have most faith in Ceska Sporitelna and Komercni Banka.
LIDOVE NOVINY - High technology exports reached 40.33 billion crowns, or 6.78 percent of all exports. This is an increase of 9.6 percent in volume.
- Intel is interested in building a factory worth $300-500 million in the Czech Republic for the manufacture and testing of microprocessors for personal computers.
